targetTexts.1: Do not envy wicked men or desire their company;
targetTexts.2: for their hearts devise violence, and their lips declare trouble.
targetTexts.3: By wisdom a house is built and by understanding it is established;
targetTexts.4: through knowledge its rooms are filled with every precious and beautiful treasure.
targetTexts.5: A wise man is strong, and a man of knowledge enhances his strength.
targetTexts.6: Only with sound guidance should you wage war, and victory lies in a multitude of counselors.
targetTexts.7: Wisdom is too high for a fool; he does not open his mouth in the meeting place.
targetTexts.8: He who plots evil will be called a schemer.
targetTexts.9: A foolish scheme is sin, and a mocker is detestable to men.
targetTexts.10: If you faint in the day of distress, how small is your strength!
targetTexts.11: Rescue those being led away to death, and restrain those stumbling toward the slaughter.
targetTexts.12: If you say, “Behold, we did not know about this,” does not He who weighs hearts consider it? Does not the One who guards your life know? Will He not repay a man according to his deeds?
targetTexts.13: Eat honey, my son, for it is good, and the honeycomb is sweet to your taste.
targetTexts.14: Know therefore that wisdom is sweet to your soul. If you find it, there is a future for you, and your hope will never be cut off.
targetTexts.15: Do not lie in wait, O wicked man, near the dwelling of the righteous; do not destroy his resting place.
targetTexts.16: For though a righteous man may fall seven times, he still gets up; but the wicked stumble in bad times.
targetTexts.17: Do not gloat when your enemy falls, and do not let your heart rejoice when he stumbles,
targetTexts.18: or the LORD will see and disapprove, and turn His wrath away from him.
targetTexts.19: Do not fret over evildoers, and do not be envious of the wicked.
targetTexts.20: For the evil man has no future; the lamp of the wicked will be extinguished.
targetTexts.21: My son, fear the LORD and the king, and do not associate with the rebellious.
targetTexts.22: For they will bring sudden destruction. Who knows what ruin they can bring?
targetTexts.23: These also are sayings of the wise: To show partiality in judgment is not good.
targetTexts.24: Whoever tells the guilty, “You are innocent”—peoples will curse him, and nations will denounce him;
targetTexts.25: but it will go well with those who convict the guilty, and rich blessing will come upon them.
targetTexts.26: An honest answer given is like a kiss on the lips.
targetTexts.27: Complete your outdoor work and prepare your field; after that, you may build your house.
targetTexts.28: Do not testify against your neighbor without cause, and do not deceive with your lips.
targetTexts.29: Do not say, “I will do to him as he has done to me; I will repay the man according to his work.”
targetTexts.30: I went past the field of a slacker and by the vineyard of a man lacking judgment.
targetTexts.31: Thorns had grown up everywhere, thistles had covered the ground, and the stone wall was broken down.
targetTexts.32: I observed and took it to heart; I looked and received instruction:
targetTexts.33: A little sleep, a little slumber, a little folding of the hands to rest,
targetTexts.34: and poverty will come upon you like a robber, and need like a bandit.
